input.title: Attested-chain fallback demo (bechina junction, LM I:13)
input.text_summary: A minimal synthetic bundle whose segment ids do NOT project in-page (project() returns null), used to exercise the explorer's stored-provenance fallback. The single hop is a real, attested aspect-identification from Likutey Moharan I:13.

hops.proof: וְשׁוֹר שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה זֶה בְּחִינַת (מִשְׁלֵי ח): "בִּי שָׂרִים יָשׂרוּ";

narrative_by_segment: This junction is attested in Likutey Moharan I:13: the 'ox' among the four creatures of the Merkavah is identified, through the verse 'through Me princes rule' (Proverbs 8:16), with rulership. The identification is a real, sourced aspect-link — but these two concepts do not project in-page, so the explorer renders the segment from its stored provenance.
narrative: A minimal demonstration of the attested-chain fallback. When a segment's concepts cannot be projected in-page, the explorer renders the segment from the bundle's stored, hop-by-hop-verified provenance — every junction still carrying its Hebrew source quote and its Likutey Moharan reference.
process_notes: Test fixture for the stored-provenance fallback. ids: c:merkavah-creatures, c:rulership. Verified in-browser that project([...]) === null for this pair (both are bechina-only, degree-1 nodes with no eitza path, so no causal projection exists in-page). The single hop is the attested bechina edge from LM I:13 (proof: Proverbs 8:16, 'bi sarim yasoru').
